We’ll soon be able to give agents a set of goals, and they can go out and design the best solution for that goal, while also continuously improving it based on the ongoing execution of whatever it built. This will obviously start with engineering because that’s where we’re seeing the best practices emerge first in almost every new era of agents.

These autonomous systems will be able to take on a set of goals, design the best outcome, test and iterate, deploy, and then optimize whatever it built on an ongoing basis. raw_text: Everybody can start making their own software, no? In some sense, the original vision of the 60s, 70s, hippie generation of computing come to life, and that's actually why Notion was started. Notion was about how do we bring this computing power to as many people as possible without forcing them to learn how to code. Hello and welcome to the Every Podcast. I'm Dan Shipper. And I'm Natalia Quintero. And this week we're talking about a conversation that you had, Dan, with Ivan Zhao, CEO and founder of Notion. Can you tell me a little bit about what you learned? Yeah, it was such an interesting conversation because Notion is the original, one of the original no code companies. The way it's structured with databases and forms and blocks, it's all designed to allow you to build something that looks kind of like software without knowing how to code. But AI like totally changed that. Now anyone can Vibe code whatever they want. You don't really need a block system. You don't really need the whole Notion interface in order to make something that looks like software. And so it kind of forced them to reinvent what they are and reinvent or rethink the original vision for their product. I've been a user of Notion for a long time, and the product has evolved quite a bit. What do you think makes Ivan the right leader to lead this transformation? You know him well. Ivan is one of those interesting people. I think there's some kind of soul overlap between Notion and Every, and I think that comes from who Ivan is as a person. You know, the way that he dresses and the way that they furnish their office, and there's so much attention to detail and so much craft in what they do. And I think that that's actually sorely missing from the... pantheon of AI CEOs. Like when you really think about what kinds of CEOs are around in this era, there are very few people who care a lot about the details and the feeling of work and what you make. And especially in a world where everyone's afraid of AI taking jobs and how do you keep the work that we do feeling human or feeling special. I think that there's something really interesting happening with Notion and Ivan is the right person to make that happen. So if you didn't catch it at thesis, let's turn over now to a conversation between Dan Shipper and Ivan Zao from Notion. Welcome, really excited to have you here. Good to be here. And thank you for sponsoring this, for making this event possible. I didn't know until I got here. Yeah, Ivan asked me backstage, he was like, how much was this? And I was like, I don't know, but next time, we'll make it bigger if you want to pay a little more. It's big enough. Good love. Great. Nice to be here. So in addition to sponsoring this conference, you make Notion. And I think of you as, we were talking about this a little bit backstage. I think there is a spiritual similarity between the way that Notion and every think about work. And I think that comes from you specifically. you think a lot...
